plan: Nine new items checked against the bank (laconic, draws on, bee association inference, turbine two-part data, parallel gerunds, 'In fact', lake-depth synthesis, coat inference, semicolon) plus S023-08 relabelled easy.

passages.title: Diary entries
passages.text: The sea captain's diary is maddeningly ______: a storm that nearly sank the ship receives a single line, and a mutiny is recorded only as "trouble with the crew."

passages.title: Stone and steel
passages.text: The architect's library ______ local tradition: it is built from the region's gray fieldstone and topped with the steep roofs of nearby farmhouses, though its glass walls and sharp angles are unmistakably modern.

passages.title: Trained bees
passages.text: Researchers trained bumblebees to find sugar water at blue disks. When the disks were then filled with plain water, the bees kept visiting them at first, but their visits dropped sharply after a few unrewarded trips. When sugar water was returned to the blue disks, visits rose again within a day. These results suggest that ______

passages.title: Turbine output
passages.text:
An engineer recorded a wind turbine's power output at different wind speeds.
Wind speed (m/s) | Output (kW)
4 | 50
8 | 400
12 | 1,450
16 | 1,500
20 | 1,500
The engineer claims that output rose steeply between 8 and 12 meters per second but leveled off at higher wind speeds.

passages.title: Island trails
passages.text: During the cleanup weekend, volunteers spent their time clearing fallen branches from the island's trails, repairing two footbridges, and ______

passages.title: Desert beetle
passages.text: The darkling beetle does not merely tolerate the heat of the Namib Desert. ______ it is most active at midday, when the sand's surface can exceed 60°C, foraging while many of its predators are sheltering from the sun.

passages.title: Two great lakes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Lake Baikal, in Russia, is the deepest lake in the world.
• Its greatest depth is about 1,640 meters.
• Lake Superior, on the border of the United States and Canada, has the largest surface area of any freshwater lake.
• Lake Superior's greatest depth is about 400 meters.

passages.title: The new coat
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story.
For three winters Nadia had worn her brother's old coat, its sleeves rolled twice at the cuffs. When her aunt finally sent money for a new one, Nadia took the bus downtown, tried on six coats, and came home with a thick blue one that fit. That night she hung it on the hook by the door, then took it down, put it on, and stood for a long time in front of the mirror in the hall.

passages.title: Glacier lake
passages.text: As the glacier retreated over the last century, meltwater collected in the hollow it left behind and formed a lake that is now more than two kilometers ______ the lake did not exist on maps made before 1930.

passages.title: Formats and genres
passages.text:
A library surveyed members about how many days they took, on average, to finish a book in print or as an audiobook.
Genre | Print (days) | Audiobook (days)
Novels | 9 | 6
Biography | 12 | 8
Poetry | 5 | 4.5
A librarian claims that audiobook listeners finished books faster than print readers in every genre, but that the difference was smallest for poetry.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: a storm that nearly sank the ship receives a single line
candidates.explanation: Entries that cover major events in a single line or a vague phrase use very few words: "laconic."

A.rationale: "Effusive" means gushing, the opposite of single-line entries.

C.rationale: "Candid" means frank; the problem is that the entries say too little, not that they are frank.

D.rationale: "Meticulous" means very careful and detailed, which the brief entries are not.

hints: How much does the diary say about major events?
candidates.remember: Match the word to the examples that follow the colon.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: built from the region's gray fieldstone and topped with the steep roofs of nearby farmhouses
candidates.explanation: The library uses traditional materials and roofs while adding modern elements, so it borrows from tradition without copying it: "draws on."

A.rationale: The building uses local stone and roof shapes, so it does not reject tradition.

B.rationale: "Imitates" suggests copying, but the glass walls and sharp angles are unmistakably modern.

C.rationale: The building clearly uses local materials and forms.

hints: Does the building copy tradition, borrow from it, or reject it?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate choices contradicted by either the traditional or the modern details.

candidates.remember: Use every detail in the sentence, including the "though" clause.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the bees adjust their visits as a color's link to a reward changes.
choices.B: bees cannot learn to associate colors with food.
choices.C: bees prefer blue to every other color, whether or not it offers food.
choices.D: plain water is more attractive to bees than sugar water is.

candidates.evidence: visits rose again within a day
candidates.explanation: Visits fell when the reward stopped and rose when it returned, so the bees track whether a color still leads to food.

B.rationale: The bees first learned to visit blue disks for sugar water.

C.rationale: Visits dropped when the blue disks held plain water.

D.rationale: Visits fell when plain water replaced sugar water.

hints: What happened each time the reward changed?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate choices contradicted by any phase of the experiment.

candidates.remember: Use all phases of an experiment, not just the first.

candidates.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the engineer's claim?

choices.A: Output was only 50 kW at 4 m/s but 1,500 kW at 20 m/s.
choices.B: Output rose sharply, from 400 to 1,450 kW, between 8 and 12 m/s.
choices.C: Output jumped from 400 to 1,450 kW at 8–12 m/s, then held near 1,500 kW.
choices.D: Output at 16 m/s was the same as output at 20 m/s.

candidates.evidence: rose steeply between 8 and 12 meters per second but leveled off
candidates.explanation: The claim has two parts. Only C shows both the steep rise (400 to 1,450) and the leveling off (1,500 at 16 and 20).

A.rationale: This shows an overall increase but neither the steep rise nor the leveling off.

B.rationale: This shows only the first part of the claim.

D.rationale: This shows only the leveling off.

hints: The claim has two parts. Which choice covers both?

strategy.explanation: Split the claim and check each choice.

candidates.remember: Choose evidence that covers every part of the claim.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: planting native shrubs along the shore.
choices.B: to plant native shrubs along the shore.
choices.C: they planted native shrubs along the shore.
choices.D: native shrubs were planted along the shore.

candidates.evidence: clearing fallen branches from the island's trails, repairing two footbridges
candidates.explanation: The series lists activities as -ing phrases ("clearing," "repairing"), so the third item must also be an -ing phrase: "planting."

B.rationale: "To plant" does not match the -ing verbs "clearing" and "repairing."

C.rationale: A new clause breaks the series of -ing phrases.

D.rationale: A passive clause breaks the parallel series.

hints: What form do the first two items in the series take?

strategy.explanation: Match the form of the earlier items.

candidates.remember: Items in a series must be parallel.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.evidence: does not merely tolerate the heat
candidates.explanation: "Does not merely tolerate" sets up a stronger claim, which the second sentence supplies: the beetle is most active in the heat. "In fact" introduces that intensification.

A.rationale: The second sentence strengthens the first rather than contrasting with it.

C.rationale: The second sentence goes further than the first; it is not a parallel example.

D.rationale: "Still" signals a concession, but nothing is being conceded.

hints: Does the second sentence contrast with the first or go further than it?
candidates.remember: "Not merely X" is often followed by "in fact, Y."

candidates.stem: The student wants to contrast the depths of the two lakes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Lake Superior has the largest surface area of any freshwater lake in the world.
choices.B: Lake Baikal, in Russia, is the deepest lake in the world.
choices.C: Lake Baikal and Lake Superior are both very large lakes in the Northern Hemisphere.
choices.D: Lake Baikal reaches about 1,640 meters deep, roughly four times Lake Superior's 400 meters.

candidates.evidence: Lake Superior's greatest depth is about 400 meters.
candidates.explanation: Only D gives both lakes' depths and compares them.

A.rationale: This gives Superior's area, not a comparison of depths.

hints: Which choice mentions the depth of both lakes?

strategy.explanation: Check each choice for both depths.

candidates.remember: A contrast needs both items and the feature being contrasted.

candidates.stem: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about Nadia?

choices.A: She takes quiet pleasure in finally owning a coat that is her own.
choices.B: She regrets spending her aunt's money on a coat.
choices.C: She plans to return the coat because it does not fit.
choices.D: She prefers her brother's coat to the new one.

candidates.evidence: then took it down, put it on, and stood for a long time in front of the mirror
candidates.explanation: After wearing a hand-me-down for three winters, Nadia puts the new coat back on and studies it in the mirror, suggesting quiet pleasure in having her own coat.

B.rationale: Nothing suggests regret; she puts the coat on again to look at it.

C.rationale: The text says the coat fit.

D.rationale: She chooses to put on the new coat and admire it.

hints: What does Nadia do after hanging up the coat?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate choices contradicted by her actions.

candidates.remember: Infer feelings from what a character does.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: the lake did not exist on maps made before 1930
candidates.explanation: Both parts are independent clauses, and a semicolon correctly joins them.

A.rationale: A comma alone cannot join two independent clauses.

B.rationale: With no punctuation, the two independent clauses run together.

hints: Is each part a complete sentence?
candidates.remember: A semicolon can join two related independent clauses.

candidates.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the librarian's claim?

choices.A: Biography took the longest in both formats: 12 days in print and 8 days as an audiobook.
choices.B: Audiobooks were faster in every genre, by 3 days for novels, 4 for biography and only 0.5 for poetry.
choices.C: Poetry took 5 days in print and 4.5 days as an audiobook, the shortest times in the table.
choices.D: Novels took 9 days in print but only 6 days as an audiobook, a difference of 3 days.

candidates.evidence: the difference was smallest for poetry
candidates.explanation: The claim has two parts: audiobooks were faster in every genre, and the gap was smallest for poetry. Only B gives all three differences and shows poetry's is the smallest.

A.rationale: This compares genres, not the size of the format difference.

C.rationale: This shows poetry was fastest overall, not that its format difference was smallest compared with the other genres.

D.rationale: This covers only one genre and says nothing about poetry.

hints: The claim has two parts. Which choice addresses both?

strategy.explanation: Split the claim, then check each choice against both parts.

candidates.remember: Evidence for a comparison across groups must include every group compared.
